subject: controlling resource by schedule and number consumed, customers not seeing consumables

messages.author: 8c246fbd7c0e1dac
messages.subject: controlling resource by schedule and number consumed, customers not seeing consumables
parts:
I've tried setting up a simple simulation where the resource is only available during a short window fixed window, and the resource can only be seized if it's available in the schedule AND if there's still a consumable resource available too. 

I've based the model off the gas-station example, but in this case it's a donut shop that's only open from 8 to 9 and only sells 12 donuts each day.  These are amazing donuts, so customers will wait as long as they have to.

I successfully made a "donut maker" that makes the 12 donuts at midnight, and this can be seen in the output:
0: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 0 old donuts on day 0
24: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 12 old donuts on day 1
48: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 11 old donuts on day 2
72: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 11 old donuts on day 3
96: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 11 old donuts on day 4
120: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 11 old donuts on day 5
144: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 11 old donuts on day 6


However the customers aren't seeing the donuts when they should be available (here's the logging for customer0 and customer1 getting their donuts):

4.76008: customer0: in line for donuts, I see 0 donuts
8: customer0: at the counter, I see 0 donuts
20.6216: customer1: in line for donuts, I see 0 donuts
24: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 12 old donuts on day 1
24: customer0: I finally got a donut after waiting for new ones
24.0167: customer0: leaving counter with my donut after 19.2565831838533 hours
27.4254: customer2: in line for donuts, I see 0 donuts
28.342: customer3: in line for donuts, I see 0 donuts
32: customer1: at the counter, I see 0 donuts
39.6982: customer4: in line for donuts, I see 0 donuts
48: controller0: made 12 donuts, discarded 11 old donuts on day 2
48: customer1: I finally got a donut after waiting for new ones
48.0167: customer1: leaving counter with my donut after 27.3950971326217 hours

If we focus on just customer0, we see:
4.76008: customer0: in line for donuts, I see 0 donuts
8: customer0: at the counter, I see 0 donuts
24: customer0: I finally got a donut after waiting for new ones
24.0167: customer0: leaving counter with my donut after 19.2565831838533 hours

In that first line, at 4.76, they get in line and should see the 12 donuts that were made at time 0.
In that second line, at 8, they should be able to seize the counter, but only if there's a donut available.  There SHOULD be a donut, but they're not seeing it, so they're waiting all the way until midnight for when the next batch is made.

Can anyone  help me figure out what am I doing wrong?  I feel confident it's in the customer trajectory, but I'm not sure how to fix it.

Thank you! 
Dale

Here's the code, essentially a stripped-down version of the gas-station example, but with a schedule added.

## Beginning of code
library(simmer)

MAX_DONUTS <- 12
NUM_DONUTS <- 0
SIM_TIME <- 24 * 7            # Simulation time in hours

NUM_DONUTS <- 0
signal <- "new donuts made"

# setup
set.seed(42)
env <- simmer()

make_donuts <- trajectory() %>%
  log_(function() {
    sim_day <- now(env) %/% 24
    old_donuts <- NUM_DONUTS
    NUM_DONUTS <<- MAX_DONUTS
    paste0("made ", NUM_DONUTS, " donuts, discarded ", old_donuts, " old donuts on day ", sim_day)
  }) %>%
  send(signal)


controller <- trajectory() %>%
  join(make_donuts) %>%
  timeout(24) %>%
  rollback(3, Inf)

customer <- trajectory() %>%
  set_attribute(c("start"), function() c(now(env))) %>%
  log_(paste0("in line for donuts, I see ", NUM_DONUTS, " donuts")) %>%
  # check if there are donuts available
  branch(function() NUM_DONUTS > 0,
         continue = TRUE,
         # if not, block until the signal "new donuts made" is received
         trajectory() %>%
           trap(signal) %>%
           wait() %>%
           log_(paste0("I finally got a donut after waiting for new ones")) %>%
           untrap(signal)
  ) %>%
  # get a donut
  seize("counter", 1) %>%
  log_(paste0(function() "at the counter, I see ", NUM_DONUTS, " donuts")) %>%
  timeout(function() {
    NUM_DONUTS <<- NUM_DONUTS -1
    return(1/60)
  }) %>%
  release("counter", 1) %>%
  log_(function()
    paste0("leaving counter with my donut after ", now(env) - get_attribute(env, "start"), " hours"))


capacity_schedule <- schedule(c(8, 9), c(1, 0), period=24)

env %>%
  add_resource("counter", capacity_schedule) %>%
  add_generator("controller", controller, at(0)) %>%
  add_generator("customer", customer, function() rexp(rate = 1/24, n = 1)) %>%
 
  run(SIM_TIME)

## End of Code

parts: Hi, thanks for the detailed description. Comments inline:

On Thu, 16 Jul 2020 at 00:51, Dale Frakes <dfr...@pdx.edu> wrote:
>
> customer <- trajectory() %>%
> set_attribute(c("start"), function() c(now(env))) %>%
> log_(paste0("in line for donuts, I see ", NUM_DONUTS, " donuts")) %>%

The "function()" is missing here, so this string is static. Mystery
solved. :) But keep reading.

> # check if there are donuts available
> branch(function() NUM_DONUTS > 0,

This should be NUM_DONUTS == 0. If there are no donuts, you enter the
branch to wait for the signal. If not, the customer just bypasses the
branch.

> continue = TRUE,
> # if not, block until the signal "new donuts made" is received
> trajectory() %>%
> trap(signal) %>%
> wait() %>%
> log_(paste0("I finally got a donut after waiting for new ones")) %>%
> untrap(signal)
> ) %>%
> # get a donut
> seize("counter", 1) %>%
> log_(paste0(function() "at the counter, I see ", NUM_DONUTS, " donuts")) %>%
Same issue as before: the "function()" should be outside.

> timeout(function() {
> NUM_DONUTS <<- NUM_DONUTS -1
> return(1/60)
> }) %>%
> release("counter", 1) %>%
> log_(function()
> paste0("leaving counter with my donut after ", now(env) - get_attribute(env, "start"), " hours"))

This is ok.

With those changes, it seems to work as expected.

--
Iñaki Úcar
